operations.evidence: The release estimates personal injury road traffic casualties in Great Britain reported by police in 2025 using the STATS19 system.
The release covers police-reported public-road casualties and is not parcel-level evidence.
The publication is labelled accredited official statistics and was independently reviewed by the Office for Statistics Regulation.
Accreditation supports statistical quality but does not make national figures suitable for exact-address scoring.
There were an estimated 1,556 road fatalities in Great Britain in 2025, 3% fewer than in 2024.
The estimate is provisional and national.
There were an estimated 29,911 killed or seriously injured casualties in 2025, 4% more than in 2024.
KSI totals do not identify risk at an individual parcel.
There were an estimated 127,870 casualties of all severities in 2025, little changed from 2024.
Police-reported casualty totals undercount some non-fatal casualties.
Motorcycle user fatalities increased 13% to 384 in 2025.
Year-to-year volatility means this change may not represent a sustained trend.
Pedestrian fatalities declined 9% to 372 in 2025.
A national road-user total cannot establish local pedestrian safety.
Pedal-cycle casualties increased 10% to 16,027 in 2025.
The total is provisional and not a route- or parcel-specific rate.
In 2025, 77% of road fatalities and 61% of casualties of all severities were male.
Population shares do not provide parcel-level exposure or causation.
The provisional release is based on police-force data supplied as of 11 May 2026.
Later validation and missing records can revise the figures.
All 40 wave54 Department for Transport source IDs are unique and use a new indexed prefix.
